title: SDK Ignite: First‑Mile Manifest (Draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact, actionable first‑mile playbook for the SDK onramp path we want to ship as the default developer experience for new users who try Redwood: 0 -> sample app running -> instrumented minimal production call. It focuses on the minimum viable steps that produce a delightful first success and telemetry capture for product/eng to iterate on.

Audience:
- New developers (engineers/ML engineers) trying Redwood for the first time
- Solutions/SEs running quick demos for customers
- Internal engineers building integrator tutorials

Goals (MVP):
1) Developer can sign up, grab API key, and run a one‑file sample in <10 minutes.
2) Sample demonstrates text generation + error handling + streaming fallback in one flow.
3) Telemetry emitted for key gate events (API key used, first successful request, latency bucketing).
4) Minimal guidance on cost/throughput (how to avoid surprise charges).
5) Hook points for placable next steps: canary config, model pinning, private deployment note.

Success metrics (first 90 days):
- 70% of signups who run the sample complete at least one successful call
- Median time to first successful call <= 9 minutes (measured by telemetry)
- Dropout reasons captured in funnel events (missing env var, quota error, auth)

Experience design constraints:
- Must work behind corp proxies; use minimal inbound ports (gateway HTTP).
- Single file sample for each language (JS, Python, curl) with clear copy/paste.
- Avoid external dependencies beyond language runtimes and official SDK.
- Include local dev mode (sdkenv that simulates responses) so offline demos possible.

First‑Mile Flow (linear):
1) Create account + copy API key (UI flow).
2) Quickstart page shows three tabs: curl, JS, Python. Each tab has runnable code and a ‘Run in Playground’ button.
3) Developer runs sample that does: a) simple prompt, b) streaming response, c) fallback to smaller model on timeout.
4) After success, inline tips show: pin a model, enable telemetry, configure caching.
5) CTA: add to repo (button to generate README snippet), open request to prod (link to Dedicated signup).

Minimal sample (JS) — copy/paste ready (pseudo but concrete):
// 1 file: sample-hello.js
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
(async ()=>{
  try{
    const res = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-creative-1', prompt: 'Summarize the last email in one line.' , stream: true, timeoutMs: 3000 });
    for await (const chunk of res.stream()) process.stdout.write(chunk.text);
    console.log('
--done--');
  } catch(e) {
    // fallback: smaller cheaper model on timeout or rate limit
    if (e.code === 'TIMEOUT' || e.code === 'RATE_LIMIT') {
      const cheap = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-small-1', prompt: 'Fallback: summarize email', stream: false });
      console.log(cheap.text);
    } else throw e;
  }
})();

Python sample snippet (single file) provided similarly in docs. Curl sample shows explicit Authorization header and minimal JSON.

Telemetry contract (minimum events):
- onboarding.started (signup -> quickstart page load)
- onboarding.key_copied (user clicked copy)
- onboarding.sample_ran (includes language tag, model used)
- inference.first_success (latency_ms, model, token_count)
- inference.fallback_used (reason)
- onboarding.completed (user clicked CTA)
Fields: anonymized_user_id, timestamp, env (prod/staging), failure_code if present. Capture as non‑PII.

Guidance: rate limits, cost guardrails
- Sample defaults to 256 token budget and warns if user attempts >1M tokens in a day.
- Inline cost estimator: milliseconds-per-token avg based on model profile.
- Recommend enabling prefix caching for chat flows (link to docs).

Developer checklist (for devx engineers shipping this):
- [ ] Finalize single-file samples for JS + Python + curl (no 3rd party libs).
- [ ] Implement telemetry events and verify in stack (analytics sandbox).
- [ ] Add 'Run in Playground' button with oauthless short‑lived token flow.
- [ ] Add local sdkenv binary that returns canned streaming chunks for demos.
- [ ] Write short security note: do not check API keys into repos; provide env var pattern.
- [ ] Add fallback wiring to sample and test in noisy network conditions (simulate loss).
- [ ] README generator for repo insertion (one button to create snippet).

Failure modes and recommended UX:
- Missing KEY: show inline help with CLI command to set env var (one line).
- Quota error: show clear message and link to pricing/quota request form.
- Network/proxy: suggest curl --proxy example and browser config.
- Streaming stalls: detect heartbeat gap > 2s and surface retry option; show fallback to non‑stream.

Localization and accessibility notes:
- Samples should be English first; keep text compact to make translations feasible.
- Ensure buttons and code blocks are keyboard accessible and include aria labels.

Next milestones (Q1 roadmap alignment):
- Week 1: lock samples and telemetry contract; wire analytics sandbox.
- Week 2: UX polish: Run in Playground + CTA flows.
- Week 3: Instrument signup funnel and run a 2‑week pilot with sales demos.
- Week 6: Iterate on dropout reasons and expand samples for a second language (Go or Ruby).

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Do we default to streaming in the sample? (Pros: show capability; Cons: fragile behind proxies)
- How aggressive should automatic fallbacks be in sample code? (teach best practice vs. hide complexity)
- Where to host sdkenv? (npm/pypi vs internal binary)

Appendix: short developer notes
- Keep sample requests small: set max_tokens=256 in examples.
- Use model names that exist in the public catalog (avoid internal beta names).
- Include unit test harness for sample to assert that fallback branch is reachable in CI.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally compact — the target is to be prescriptive and minimal. Please leave comments inline in Confluence doc linked above for any UX copy changes or code portability concerns.
- If we agree on telemetry fields, Product will wire the funnel dashboard and SRE will add a latency SLO tag for onboarding.sample_ran.

Author: Asha Patel (eng-developer-experience) — draft for internal review.
